title: The Secure Bond and Dealing with Tantrums with Rifq
summary: This lesson addresses 'the secure bond and dealing with tantrums with rifq (gentleness)' for children from two to three years old. No, practice 'the 30-second response.' Respond to his call immediately, even if just with a reassuring word. Quick response builds 'secure attachment' and makes the child feel safe, while ignoring causes him chronic stress. Expect tantrums because they are natural. Take a deep breath, use a calm voice, and say to him: 'I am here with you, you are safe.' You can try to distract him or give him time to calm down on his own without getting upset yourself. Dedicate minutes daily for full presence without screens or phones. Sit on the floor, make eye contact, smile at him, and imitate his sounds. This physical and heartfelt presence builds his confidence in himself and in the world around him.

reflection_prompts: My infant cries constantly. Should I leave him to cry to avoid spoiling him with excessive pampering?
My child is having a tantrum and refuses to stop screaming. How do I handle this with rifq?

review_defects.arabic: هل أتركه يبكي لتجنب إفساده بالدلال؟
review_defects.english: Should I leave him to cry to avoid spoiling him with excessive pampering?
review_defects.why: The Arabic says 'إفساده بالدلال' (spoiling him with pampering) without qualification. The English adds 'excessive', which changes the meaning by implying that only excessive pampering is harmful, whereas the Arabic suggests pampering itself could spoil.
